goalInOwnWords: Build a line of machines that turns scrap into things worth more, ship enough to fill each order, earn stars, and try to beat the foreman's score.
stoppedWhere: Home screen after the survey, having left today's yard (Beams for the hospital wing) halfway through: 3 of 6 orders filled, $4,359, just before the scrap truck at shift 4.
stoppedWhy: I had gone well past the quarter hour I was asked for and halfway through a real yard felt like a natural place to rest my eyes. I liked it, but I would put it down now and come back another morning with my coffee.

stuck.where: Lesson 1, second pick (Furnace) and later picks, shelf under the yard
stuck.what: Sal said tap the Furnace, but the parts on the shelf change places each time, so my habit of tapping the first box picked the spare belt piece instead.
stuck.gotOutHow: Looked at the shelf again, saw the Furnace in the second box and tapped that.

stuck.what: The note said the furnace held me back and a Tuner or a second furnace would clear it, but the cards offered had no Tuner and the second-furnace card said no spot pays more yet, so I could not tell which card was right.
stuck.gotOutHow: Trusted the green tag Fits this line now and took the Hopper kit; it worked ($1,995) but I do not know if it was the clever choice.

confused: Lesson 1: Sal said the line was closed while the Crusher and Furnace were still shown as not ticked, and the shift was said to pay $37 when ingots were $24 each (it was plain scrap at $1).
Why a spare Crusher, spare Furnace or spare Dock sat on the shelf unused until Sal finally pointed at it.
Nobody said why I was asked to tap a Conveyor right after picking the Hopper (Lesson 2).
The note on every shift in today's yard, You're level with Sal. He builds a shift at a time and never moves a machine: plan ahead, or rearrange, meant nothing to me.
On the first real job card: what an order is exactly (one per shift?), the scrap truck, and marked spots, all at once.
The little panels with Turn right, Turn left, Move and Back to the shelf: I was afraid of lifting my part up and losing my place.
The picture of the belt looked broken near the Tuner in Lesson 3 although money was coming in.
annoyed: Shelf boxes change order, so I cannot tap from memory.
Text at the bottom of the build panel was partly hidden behind buttons (if every shift pays this).
A lot of words on the job card for today's yard.
I never felt I made a clever choice myself; the tags decided for me.
pleased: Sal telling me exactly one thing to do at a time, so I never felt lost.
The forecast before every shift (This shift will pay $576, up $465) and it being right to the dollar.
The red label on a machine saying held you back or waiting for scrap, which showed me the problem instead of lecturing.
Each lesson ending with one plain sentence I can remember.
Home saying my game is saved and asking before replacing it; Undo being there.
Buying a belt explained honestly as coming out of my score.
bestMoment: The end of Lesson 3: ingots at $24 piling up, three stars filled, and the line I had arranged with a Tuner and a Splitter actually working.
worstMoment: Starting today's yard: a wall of new words and a choice of three cards with no way to know which was right, plus a boast from Sal I could not use.
oneChange: Let me make one choice on my own and tell me afterwards whether it was a good one, in plain words, and drop the lines comparing me to Sal.
